general quota, and the succeeding quotas will be based on the yield at the shipping point, on 65 per cent of the wheat acreage of 1940.

speakerposition: Minister of National War Services; Minister of Agriculture
subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext: If you want to take that, take it. I will not argue further.

subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext: But the point is that this table suggested that the man with a 25-bushel yield can market 19-54 bushels to the acre. I have told the people in my constituency that all they can hope to sell will be twelve bushels on sixty-five per cent of the 1940 acreage. If the Minister of Trade and Commerce tells friends of those who heard the hon. member for Acadia that they can deliver nineteen bushels in my constituency, I shall be in difficulties, and I think the Minister of Trade and Commerce should make a statement to-morrow to indicate that either the Minister of Agriculture is wrong or that he was wrong on April 8.

speakerposition: Minister of National War Services; Minister of Agriculture
subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext:
I think I understand
what my hon. friend is trying to do. He is trying to get it absolutely on the record that if they can deliver more than twelve bushels next fall, the Minister of Agriculture is to blame for saying they could not. It is proper to say that, I suppose, after it is all over, but I have said all I have to say.

subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext:
Stop being
suspicious.

subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext: I resent the suggestion made by the Minister of Agriculture.

speakerposition: Minister of National War Services; Minister of Agriculture
subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext: I have been through it so often I know pretty well what the hon. member has in mind.

subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext: I had a dozen meetings while I was away, and I explained these regulations to my constituents, who are busy on the land at the present time. If I have been mistaken in my explanation, I am anxious to correct it so that they may have a chance at once-

speakerposition: Minister of National War Services; Minister of Agriculture
subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext: I will not correct mine.

subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext: Well, the Minister of Trade and Commerce should make a statement to-morrow.

subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext: I have one question to ask with reference to the definitions. In southern Alberta quite a number of farmers are growing mustard, and in one district at least fifty are going in for soya beans. Would mustard and soya beans be considered coarse grains?

speakerposition: Minister of National War Services; Minister of Agriculture
subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext:
No, not under the
definitions as they are, and they will not be changed.

subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext: Many hon. members have something more to say and a few questions to ask. I was going to come to the minister's rescue in connection with this quota delivery, but it is eleven o'clock.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext: I hope that to-morrow we may pass this item, but I cannot speak for others. I should like to ask the Minister of Trade and Commerce for some definite information with respect to the wheat board, which I think the country is entitled to know-that is, with regard to the amount of cash wheat being carried by the board, the amount of wheat carried in other ways, the obligations of the board to the banks, and what-not. The true position should be put on the record. The Minister of Mines and Resources shakes his head. There is no such situation existing to-day as there was at the time of the McFarland operations, and there is no similar reason why we should not have the information. There is no question of competition or of price cutting or anything else. There is only one buyer, and the situation is known. Parliament is entitled to have that information, and I give notice now.

speakerposition: Minister of National War Services; Minister of Agriculture
subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext: With regard to that, to-night and ever since this item has been before the committee, I think that both the chairman and I have allowed far too much latitude in the discussion. As a matter of fact, the information asked for has nothing whatever to do with this estimate. It comes under trade and commerce, and I do not know why I, as Minister of Agriculture, in getting an estimate through, should be asked for information having to do with trade and commerce. I shall have to ask the chairman to see that the matter is not discussed until this item is through.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext:
If that
is a threat, the minister will not get his estimates through very quickly.

speakerposition: Minister of National War Services; Minister of Agriculture
subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext: The threat came from the other side of the house.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext:
Let us
approach this in a spirit of good-will, and the minister will get his estimates through much sooner. I suggest to him that there is a first-class argument as to why the position of the wheat board with respect to wheat should be given to the committee under this estimate, which relates to wheat.

speakerposition: Minister of National War Services; Minister of Agriculture
subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext:
There is no argument whatever that I know of as to why we should discuss the estimates of trade and commerce

British Columbia Telephone Company
under the estimates of agriculture. There is no argument at all, and no rule that permits it.

subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext: The first order in council stated that you were taking only 230,000,000 bushels of wheat, and that is the reason for these regulations.

speakerposition: Minister of National War Services; Minister of Agriculture
subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext: But that has to do with trade and commerce; it has nothing at all to do with agriculture.

subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext: It was presented to the house by the two ministers as a joint policy.

speakerposition: Minister of National War Services; Minister of Agriculture
subtopic: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDER 28 THIS DAY TO PERMIT DEBATE ON MOTION OF MR. ILSLEY FOR COMMITTEE OF SUPPLY
speechtext:
Hon. members will have an opportunity to discuss that when the other matter comes up.
Progress reported.
